name: Rice Pudding With Eggs
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: Handful of raisins, seeded and cut in two
ingredients.originalText: Handful of raisins, seeded and cut in two

instructions.text: Soak the rice in a pint of the milk an hour, then set the saucepan containing it where it will slowly heat to a boil.
Boil five minutes; remove and let it cool.
Beat the yolks, add the sugar and butter, the rice and the milk in which it was cooked, with the pint of unboiled; the beaten whites, and finally the raisins.
Grate nutmeg on the top, and bake three-quarters of an hour, or until the custard is well set and of a light brown.

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Soak the rice in a pint of the milk an hour, then set the saucepan containing it where it will slowly heat to a boil.
2. Boil five minutes; remove and let it cool.
3. Beat the yolks, add the sugar and butter, the rice and the milk in which it was cooked, with the pint of unboiled; the beaten whites, and finally the raisins.
4. Grate nutmeg on the top, and bake three-quarters of an hour, or until the custard is well set and of a light brown.
5. Eat cold.
